claims: The northern lights are also known as aurora borealis.
Aurora borealis are caused by solar wind interacting with Earth’s magnetic field.
Aurora borealis are typically visible in high-latitude regions.
Northern lights are best viewed from August to April.
Northern lights are best viewed in dark northern locations such as Alaska Canada and Norway.
Northern lights appear as green pink or purple lights 80–500 km up.
Auroras are caused by charged particles from the sun colliding with gases in Earth’s upper atmosphere.
The best time to see northern lights is between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m. local time.
Peak viewing months for northern lights are around the spring and fall equinoxes in March and September.
Northern lights are most commonly seen in aurora ovals around the North and South Poles.
Northern lights are typically seen between 60 and 75 degrees latitude.
Northern lights can appear as stationary glows.
Northern lights can appear as moving dancing curtains of light.
Northern lights can appear in colors like pale green pink red yellow blue and violet.
Northern lights activity can be monitored via the NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center.
